title: [Chapitre] VI. Analysis situs (deuxième mouture) : notes manuscrites (18-20/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: in 'Analysis situs, deuxième mouture' (June 1986) Grothendieck is building an order-theoretic axiomatics for a set 𝔉 of 'figures': cellular, presumably tame, decompositions of subsets of a space, with a least element ∅_𝔉, the empty figure. On p. 11 he introduced six relations: four orders ⊲, ≤, ≼, ≪ and two symmetric relations ∥ and ≬. The intended meanings, inferred from pp. 11-13, are:
- ≤: sub-figure (subcomplex).
- ⊲: 'X is a cell of F'. The set 𝓜 of cells consists of the strictly join-irreducible elements for ≤, and the 'déploiement' F̃ = {X ∈ 𝓜 | X ⊲ F} gives F ≤ G ⇔ F̃ ⊂ G̃. This is a Birkhoff-type representation, worked out on p. 11.
- ≼: subdivision.
- ≪: refinement. In the first draft it was defined as G ≪ F ⇔ ∃F' with G ≤ F' ≼ F, i.e. G is a subfigure of a subdivision of F.
- ∥: disjointness. F ∥ F holds only for F = ∅.
- ≬: a reflexive 'compatibility' relation between cell structures.

This page asks which of these relations determine which, so as to choose a minimal set of primitive data.

(a) [Ends the p. 11 remark] The structure can be fixed by taking either ≤ or ⊲ as principal.

(b) Each of ≤ and ≪ determines ∥ (1.24):
- F ∥ G ⇔ {F,G} has an upper bound for ≤ and Inf_≤(F,G) = ∅.
- F ∥ G ⇔ Sup_≪(F,G) exists and Inf_≪(F,G) = ∅.
He marks (1.24) 'vérifier' and notes that ∅_𝔉 is the least element for both ≤ and ≪.

(c) ≪ determines the subdivision relation (written ≲ here) by (1.25): F ≲ G ⇔ F ≪ G and, for all H, (H ∥ F ⇔ H ∥ G), with ∥ obtained from ≪ via (b). In other words, a subdivision is a refinement with the same support. Support is detected purely through disjointness, which is a point-free way of saying |F| = |G|.

(d) ≪ determines 𝓛 (1.26), the set of minimal elements of 𝔉∖{∅}, i.e. nonempty figures whose only nonempty refinement is themselves. These are presumably the points / 0-cell figures.

He then states that he does not see how ≪ (or ≪ together with ≲, 'c'est kif-kif') could determine ≤, or even ≬. A crossed-out attempt to derive ≬ from ≪ is abandoned.

(e) ≪ and ≬ together determine ≤ (1.27): G ≤ F ⇔ G ≪ F and G ≬ F. A refinement-subfigure whose cell structure is compatible with F is an honest subcomplex.

The next page lists the possible primitive pairs: (≤,≪), (≤,≼), (≪,≬). He explains that the first draft used (≤,≼), but he now switches to (≤,≪) as technically simplest, and regards (≪,≬) as a curiosity. The page thus serves to choose the axiomatic primitives for a lattice-theoretic ('point-free') theory of tame cell structures, a foundation for the 'géométrie modérée' of the Esquisse.
errors: (1.24b) is flagged 'vérifier' by Grothendieck himself. The role of the existence of Sup_≪(F,G) is unclear. For disjoint figures a common refinement-supremum should exist, but whether every pair with Inf_≪ = ∅ automatically has a sup, or conversely, depends on axioms not yet stated. The equivalence is a conjecture at this point rather than a proven fact.
Equation number (1.27) is used twice: once for the crossed-out attempt and once for the final formula in e).

The meaning of ≬ is never defined on this page. (1.27) is only correct if ≬ means compatibility of cell structures (union or overlap is a subfigure of a common figure); with a mere 'intersect' meaning it would fail.

On p. 11 ≪ is called an order relation. Antisymmetry of ≪ (refinement both ways implies equality) is assumed, not checked; the next page admits that transitivity and reflexivity of ≪ were laborious in the first draft.

ideas.what: Recovering the cell-complex structure from the join-irreducibles of the subcomplex order (𝓜 = strictly irreducible elements, déploiement F̃) — completed on p. 11 and referred to at the top of this page
ideas.modern_name: Birkhoff representation of a distributive lattice by its join-irreducibles; face poset of a regular CW complex
ideas.usually_credited_to: G. Birkhoff (1937); face posets: Björner (1984) and others

ideas.what: Disjointness expressed lattice-theoretically: bounded pair with infimum ∅ (1.24)
ideas.modern_name: disjointness / orthogonality in a lattice with 0

ideas.what: Subdivision defined as refinement with the same 'disjointness profile' (1.25), giving a point-free characterization of equal support
ideas.modern_name: subdivision as support-preserving refinement; essentially point-free (locale-style) definition of 'same underlying set'
ideas.usually_credited_to: PL topology (subdivision) — the specific order-theoretic characterization is not standard

ideas.what: Points as minimal nonempty elements for refinement (1.26)
Which primitive relations suffice: (≤,≪), (≤,≼), (≪,≬); subcomplex = refinement + compatibility (1.27)
ideas.modern_name: axiomatics of tame/PL cell structures via orders (in the spirit of the Esquisse's 'géométrie modérée')
ideas.usually_credited_to: Esquisse d'un programme §5 (tame topology programme, 1984); o-minimal cell decomposition (van den Dries, Knight–Pillay–Steinhorn) as later realization
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme only announces tame topology; this order-theoretic axiomatics does not appear there as far as I know

missed.claim: An order-theoretic, point-free axiomatization of the category of tame cellular figures, using refinement ≪ and sub-figure ≤ as primitives, from which subdivision, disjointness, cells and points are derived. It is left unproved here (marked 'vérifier'), and the definability question is left open: ≪ alone does not determine ≤.
missed.quote: Je ne vois pas que ≪ (+ ≲, c'est kif-kif) détermine ≤, ni même ≬.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Tame topology is now done via o-minimal structures, which are point-set and model-theoretic. A purely order-theoretic axiomatics of cell structures with refinement and subdivision is a different foundational route. A precise definability question of this kind (is ≤ definable from ≪?) could be posed for o-minimal cell decompositions or for PL face posets. This is modest but apparently unexplored.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is foundational bookkeeping: inter-definability of relations among figures. The individual facts are routine lattice theory. The interest lies only in the overall unpublished project (axiomatic tame topology via orders, 1986), which is documented on surrounding pages. The specific characterization of subdivision via disjointness profile is a nice detail but not a significant result.
transcription_corrections: The relation in c) and in the 'kif-kif' remark is drawn as ≼ with a wavy lower stroke (≲-like). It is the subdivision relation called ≼ on pp. 11 and 13, not a new relation.
The margin note 'vérifier →' is attached to (1.24), and '×' marks appear in the margin at (1.25) and at the final (1.27).

The parenthetical after (1.26) reads roughly '(Cela signifie une figure non vide dont le seul raffinement non vide est elle-même)'. It describes the minimal elements as nonempty figures whose only nonempty refinement is themselves, not '...dans la seule raffinement...'.
In (1.24b) 'Sup' is written over a crossed-out word, with subscript ≪, and 'Inf' carries subscript ≪; in (1.24a) Inf carries superscript ≤.
